answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon publishes fresh challenge words — say onyx, falcon, sonnet — and agents must incorporate them correctly into real-time responses tied to the task at hand. Precomputed template answers become useless because nobody could know the words in advance. An attacker wanting N fake identities must run N distinct reasoning processes per epoch, paying compute and latency costs for every sybil account every round, which quickly exceeds the value of any single-identity reward.
